raw_response: DESCRIPTION: This plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) of several methods as a function of co-occurrence number. The x-axis represents "Co-occurrence Number" on a logarithmic scale, ranging from approximately 3 to over 3000, with tick marks at 10^1, 10^2, and 10^3. The y-axis represents "ACC (%)" on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 35% to 65%, with tick marks at 5% intervals. Six lines are shown, each representing a different method. The black line with circle markers ("Base") starts at approximately 37% at the lowest co-occurrence number, rises slightly to around 43.5% at co-occurrence number ~30, and then remains relatively flat at approximately 43.5% through the highest co-occurrence values. The light blue line with downward-triangle markers ("FT") begins at approximately 39.5%, increases gradually, and reaches about 47.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. The red line with upward-triangle markers ("IKE") starts at approximately 43% and rises steadily to about 49% at the highest co-occurrence number. The brown line with diamond markers ("MEND") begins at approximately 44.5%, increases to around 49% at co-occurrence ~30, continues rising to approximately 54% at co-occurrence ~300, and reaches about 56.5% at the highest value. The purple line with pentagon markers ("MEMIT") starts at approximately 43.5%, rises to about 51% at co-occurrence ~30, increases to approximately 53% at co-occurrence ~300, and reaches about 54.5% at the highest co-occurrence number. The green line with square markers ("ROME") begins at approximately 51%, shows a steady upward trend through approximately 57% at co-occurrence ~30 and 62% at co-occurrence ~300, and reaches the highest value of approximately 65.5% at the largest co-occurrence number. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence numbers, while Base consistently shows the lowest values.
